evidence.name: Screen Editor action button
evidence.userNeed: Set the action button label/behavior so the next step is clear and the canvas transition matches it; keep required inputs blocking.

sections.title: Set the primary button label
sections.description: The primary button text is the visible call-to-action (Continue, Next, Subscribe). Make it reflect the screen goal so visitors know what happens on click.

sections.title: Control primary button visibility
sections.description: Toggle the primary button on or off. Hide it when visitors must interact with the content first; at least one of the primary or secondary buttons must stay visible.

sections.title: Style the primary button
sections.description: Apply text and button styling through five accordion groups: Container (padding), Gradient, Shadow, Effects, and Icon. Strong styling makes the button read as the important next step.

sections.title: Add an optional secondary button
sections.description: Enable and label a secondary action (Skip, Learn More, Log In) for an alternative path. Keep it less prominent than the primary; use it for exits, not the main goal.

sections.title: Control secondary button visibility
sections.description: When the secondary button is enabled, toggle it visible or hidden. Hide it to force commitment to the primary action only.

sections.title: Style the secondary button
sections.description: Style the secondary button with the same five accordion groups but lower visual priority (softer colors, lighter weight) to preserve the hierarchy.

sections.title: Understand button layout
sections.description: Buttons stack vertically or horizontally based on width and theme, with the primary always before the secondary. Layout is automatic, so focus on labels and styling.
